subject.title: Support Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk via gateway relay

question: Should Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk be implemented now as an OpenAI-provider server-side Gateway Relay path, and which Azure auth modes are in scope for the first landing?
rationale: The code path touches provider auth, browser-vs-server credential boundaries, Azure endpoint selection, SecretRef guidance, and live cloud proof; automation should not choose that security/product boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: API-key relay first
options.body: Land a narrow API-key-only Azure Gateway Relay path with no browser credential exposure, explicit Azure diagnostics, docs, tests, and live proof when quota is available; leave Entra ID as a follow-up.

options.title: Full Azure auth now
options.body: Require the first implementation to include both API-key and Microsoft Entra ID/managed identity support, accepting a larger design and validation cycle before users get Azure Talk.

options.title: Defer until live quota
options.body: Keep the issue open but defer implementation until maintainers have a deployable Azure GPT Realtime resource for end-to-end proof before designing the permanent path.

recommendation.title: API-key relay first
recommendation.body: Land a narrow API-key-only Azure Gateway Relay path with no browser credential exposure, explicit Azure diagnostics, docs, tests, and live proof when quota is available; leave Entra ID as a follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history for the OpenAI realtime provider and Talk docs points to steipete's merged GA bridge work and current-main import/provenance on the relevant files.
